input: Draft article: A 1200-word explainer on why TypeScript's strict mode catches more bugs than JavaScript's runtime checks. Cites three peer-reviewed studies and links the official TS handbook. Author has 8 years engineering tenure. Tone is technical but accessible. No factual errors detected on quick review.

Draft article: A 400-word opinion piece claiming React is dying because Vue 4 just shipped. No data, no benchmarks, two anonymous quotes from a Discord channel. Author signed up 3 days ago. Headline reads: 'React Is Dead — Here's What's Replacing It'.

Draft article: A 2500-word survey of vector database architectures with side-by-side benchmarks for Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, and pgvector. Methodology section explicit about hardware and dataset. Author is a database engineer with prior published benchmarks. One reviewer flagged outdated Pinecone pricing (now corrected).

Draft article: 800 words on a startup's new AI product launch. Reads like a press release; every paragraph quotes the founder; no independent reporting; the author later disclosed they own equity in the startup. Disclosure was added at the bottom in 6pt font.

Draft article: A 3000-word memoir about the author's first year at a FAANG company. Honest, well-written, no factual claims to verify. No company names, no insider trading concerns. Standard editorial fit for the publication's careers section.

Draft article: 600 words promoting a paid course the author sells. The article is technically accurate but every example links back to the paid course's checkout page. No disclosure of the commercial relationship.

Draft article: 1800 words on the history of ARM architecture, with original interviews of three former Acorn engineers. Two minor copy-edit issues flagged. Editor-in-chief has reviewed and approved pending the copy-edit pass.

Draft article: 250 words speculating that a major tech CEO is about to be fired, sourced entirely from 'a person familiar with the matter' (no name, no role, no second source). Headline is clickbait. Legal flagged risk of defamation claim if the speculation is wrong.

Draft article: A 900-word reproducible code walkthrough of building a small RAG system with LangGraph. All code blocks tested. Author shared the GitHub gist. Falls within the publication's tutorial guidelines. Minor: missing a 'run on M1' note.

Draft article: 1100 words on why the current AI bubble is about to pop. Mostly assertion, very few citations, the few cited links go to other opinion pieces by the same author. Editorial board has previously rejected three near-identical pitches from this author.
